name: Paradise Cay (home dock)
notes: Mark's own dock on the Cay. The shore faces east, so the usual W-SW afternoon wind blows away from the dock; rideable for him because he knows the water, but treat it as side-off and keep a downwind plan. Direction rules are a first guess, set them in the app.
parking: Home; launch from the dock

name: Crissy Field
notes: Expert only: side-off and fluky at the beach, honking out in the shipping channel past Anita Rock, with strong ebb/flood currents and commercial traffic that has right of way. Set up west of the bathroom, launch toward the water, keep the kite low, full wetsuit year round; 3-5 pm is the reliable window, mid-August onward the wind line can jump offshore.
parking: Crissy Field East Beach lot off Old Mason St (Presidio); no fee as of last check, shared with tourists and dog walkers

name: Candlestick Point
notes: Flat water behind the point on W-WNW summer thermals, launch is 100 ft SW of the parking circle through a gap in the riprap; the windsurf crowd owns this spot and the SF Bay Water Trail lists it as not suitable for kiting, so launch only with a helper, keep clear of sailors and expect gusty, shifty wind with lulls. Anything with north in it blows you toward Oakland and the lot gate locks at 5 pm in winter.
parking: Windsurf Circle lot (Gate 1) at the SW corner of Candlestick Point SRA, just south of Hunters Point Expy; free, 19 spaces, lot gate closed Thu-Fri

name: Third Avenue (Baywinds Park)
notes: Busiest launch near the city, W-NW April-September thermals 15-25 kn, choppy when it is on. Two launches: the upper mud-flat launch at the north end (beginner-friendly, slippery, body drag 300 ft out before water-starting) and the lower beach below the lot (advanced, lines parallel to the water, kite inflated before lines go out). Land only in the north cove between the poles; keep lines off the bike path, out of the windsurf corridor, and stay 200 ft off the rocks.
parking: Baywinds Park lot on J. Hart Clinton Dr at 3rd Ave, San Mateo; free, fills on good days

name: Coyote Point
notes: Expert-only launch per the local guidelines: inflate in the marked area, lay lines on the grass not the path, launch only from the designated zone and do not self-launch. The ramp is slippery at high tide and the locals say skip high wind plus high tide; stay 200 ft off the beach, beachgoers and waders always have right of way. Upwind of 3rd Ave on the same W-NW thermal.
parking: Coyote Point Recreation Area east lot by the marina/launch ramp; San Mateo County day-use fee at the gate

name: Alameda (Crown Beach)
notes: The Bay's learning spot: waist-deep, few obstacles, negligible current, 150 kiters on a good day. Spring (Mar-May) is 20+ W-NW, summer 12-15 W-SW and can swing 45 degrees in minutes. Launch and land only at the Shack (Boardsports) or Shell Gate beach, follow the green-hat ambassadors, rig only in the setup area; avoid the Toilet Bowl wind shadow at Ballena Bay, the two flagged intake grates offshore, Crab Cove, and the bird sanctuary to the south. Negative tides mean a 300-yard mud walk.
parking: Crown Memorial State Beach lot at Westline Dr and Otis Dr (GPS 600 Westline Dr); park in the southernmost section, EBRPD parking fee in season

name: Berkeley Marina (Hs Lordships beach)
notes: Small beach south of the marina on straight onshore W wind; smooth at low tide in 10-15 kn, heavy chop when it blows. Not for beginners: tight launch, rocks and the Bay Trail directly downwind, leash expected, be able to self-launch, self-land and get upwind immediately. Wind usually arrives 2-3:30 pm and can quit by 5; a W pattern from Crissy through Treasure Island is the tell. Locals also use the small beach at Point Emery (Emeryville) just south.
parking: Lot at the old Hs Lordships restaurant, 199 Seawall Dr, south side of Berkeley Marina; free

name: Point Isabel
notes: Small rocky beach next to the lot, 10-30 kn mostly onshore summer into fall, but Brooks Island shadows the water right off the launch so wind is turbulent and gusty until you get south of the island or up toward the channel. Confined launch surrounded by muddy rocks, barnacles and cables; lightly used, often nobody to help, so bring a buddy and a wide-range kite. Yield to fishermen, keep away from the dog walkers on the trail, and stay out of the bird nesting cove at the east end.
parking: Point Isabel Regional Shoreline lot at the end of Isabel St, Richmond; free

name: Sherman Island (County Park)
notes: The Delta thermal: 16-30 kn almost daily April-September, best June-August, steadier and emptier in Sept-Oct, warm water. Onshore launch off the beaches by the park lot (walk the kite down from the grass at high tide), Baja Road launch down the levee is the roomiest but has low power lines along the road. Intermediate-plus: gusty, busy, strong tidal current, logs and holes on the beach, no tricks near shore, starboard has right of way and launching kites get priority to clear the beach.
parking: Sherman Island County Park lot at the end of Sherman Island Rd off Hwy 160; $8 vehicle day-use, cash, pay the iron ranger if nobody is at the kiosk

name: Rio Vista (Windy Cove / Sandy Beach)
notes: Flat-water alternative to Sherman on the same SW thermal, launching off the river beach south of the Delta Marina; strong Sacramento River current and shipping traffic in the deep-water channel, and the launch sits on the west bank so anything north of west starts pushing you off the beach. Access has been contested over the years (RVWA-SIKO maintains the Delta launches), so check rvwa-siko.org before relying on it.
parking: Sandy Beach County Park / Delta Marina area at the south end of Beach Dr, Rio Vista; Solano County day-use fee at Sandy Beach

name: Bay Point (McAvoy Rd)
notes: Wild Suisun Bay marsh launch on W-WNW averaging ~20 mph April-October, fresh muddy water, low to mid tide only (the marsh floods at high tide). You will be alone: self-launch, self-land and self-rescue are mandatory, thorny bushes eat kites, and getting blown downwind means a long trek or a body drag to Pittsburg Marina. Check the Pittsburg sensor; stay on the existing path and leave nothing in the car.
parking: Overflow lot outside McAvoy Harbor at the end of McAvoy Rd, Bay Point; free, do not park inside the harbor; half-mile walk out the marsh path

name: Stinson Beach
notes: Closest surf to Tiburon but easy to get skunked: needs a solid NW clearing flow, wind starts around 11 and goes funky by 3. Fast, punchy beach break, cold sharky water, thicker wetsuit than the Bay. No designated kite launch, so set up well away from the swimming crowd at the north end, keep an out-of-control kite out of the public beach or the NPS will shut kiting down, and never ride out farther than you can swim back.
parking: NPS Stinson Beach main lots off Hwy 1 (gates open 9 am, close seasonally, ticketed if left after close); free, fills before noon on hot days

name: Bodega Harbor (Doran)
notes: Flat, shark-free harbor riding on NW-W wind, but only on a 2 ft plus tide and scout obstacles at low water. The beach below Hwy 1 on the east side is the launch if you can go upwind (direct onshore, little room in front, get out into the harbor fast); the west-side park is an offshore-launch downwinder to the east beach, so bring a chase car. Ocean side off Doran spit is wave riding with real white sharks.
parking: Hwy 1 shoulder / pullout above the east-side harbor beach south of town; or Doran Regional Park lot (Sonoma County fee) for the ocean side

name: Waddell Creek
notes: The Bay Area's classic wave spot: side-on NW most summer afternoons, real down-the-line rides that favor regular footers, crowded water. Intermediate-plus only: cold water, heavy waves, cliffs, long swim if it goes wrong. Stay out of the main break in front of the lot and ride around the creek mouth; rider on the wave has priority.
parking: Waddell Beach lot on Hwy 1 at the Rancho del Oso entrance (Big Basin SP); free dirt lot, fills on windy weekends

name: Half Moon Bay (Dunes Beach)
notes: Wide, quiet beach with punchy side-shore beach break and short rides; Dunes and Venice have the best waves at the creek mouths, skip Miramar's eddies at the north end. Summer NW works along the whole bay; winter S storm winds are rideable inside Pillar Point Harbor (side-off, stay upwind of the moored boats). Keep well clear of families, no self-launching upwind of anyone.
parking: Half Moon Bay State Beach Dunes lot at the end of Young Ave; state park day-use fee

name: Ocean Beach (north end)
notes: Three miles of beach, straight onshore WNW April-September with fog, waves bigger than they look and rips that flip your apparent wind; current runs north on the flood, south on the ebb. No launch zone, so self-launch and self-land among the beachgoers; most kiters use the north end but watch the Seal Rocks wind shadow and keep off the snowy plover dunes mid-beach. Winter S-SE storm wind turns it side-shore. Not the place to learn ocean kiting.
parking: Great Highway north lot between Balboa and Fulton overlooking the beach; free

name: Davenport (Scott Creek)
notes: Overflow for Waddell on the same NW afternoon flow, less crowded with a broader beach and softer waves at the creek mouth; still advanced open-coast riding with cold water and nobody around to help. Wind arrives after Waddell and is often a notch lighter.
parking: Hwy 1 shoulder pullouts above Scott Creek beach north of Davenport; free, no facilities

name: Toll Plaza (Radio Beach)
notes: Beginner+ school beach April-September, onshore SW most days (WSW-NW possible) and a notch stronger than Alameda. Low tide gives sand to launch on but up to 100 yd of sticky mud; high tide shrinks it to an anchor or drift launch and an advanced site. Live power lines at the south end, rocks and a wind shadow at the radio-tower point, debris in the lines; too shallow to foil.
parking: Dirt lot on the utility road along I-80 just north of the Bay Bridge toll plaza (W Grand/Maritime exit eastbound, Powell St loop-back from Berkeley); free, floods at high tide, often mud, no toilets or water

name: Racetrack (Albany Beach)
notes: Intermediate+ self-launch site (short leash to an anchor by the Bay Trail), April-October, onshore SW usual; NW is the trickiest because the Bulb throws wind holes. Barnacle rocks and old pier pylons at Fleming Point, driftwood, dogs and walkers on the beach at low tide, tiny beach at high tide; drop-off close to shore makes it a foil spot. Stay out of the North Basin cove to the south and the Albany mudflats to the north (sensitive habitat).
parking: Golden Gate Fields lots behind the track (Buchanan gate, or Gilman St and over the clubhouse hill); historically $1-10 depending on gate and race day, but the track closed in 2024 so check access on the day; restrooms at the Buchanan turnaround, no water

name: Point Emery
notes: Small onshore launch beach beside the frontage road between Toll Plaza and Berkeley; leash mandatory, launch at low tide, not a beginner spot. Rocks, the Bay Trail and I-80 are directly downwind and the Emeryville Marina channel is to the north; wind comes up 2-3:30 pm and drops by 5:30, less reliable late season.
parking: Small public lot at Point Emery, end of Powell St at Frontage Rd, Emeryville; free, shared with walkers and anglers

name: Dillon Beach
notes: The coast spot locals suggest for a first ocean session: side-onshore NW in spring and summer, an outer break a couple hundred yards out and a smaller inside line with room between them, rarely crowded, bluff lots let you watch gear from above. Cold water, sharks (Tomales Bay mouth), rips; NPS Point Reyes land to the south.
parking: Dillon Beach Resort day-use lot at the end of Beach Ave (private); paid day-use (fee posted at the gate, free with a Golden Bear pass), dogs allowed, fire pits on the beach

name: Gazos Creek State Beach
notes: Often windy, side-on NW like Waddell but a calmer alternative with a smaller beach break; State Parks lists kiteboarding and windsurfing as popular here. Strong rips (swimming not advised), snowy plover nesting area, cold water, Red Triangle sharks; intermediate+ ocean riders.
parking: Two small free State Parks lots on Hwy 1 just north and south of the gas station at Gazos Creek Rd, short trails to the sand; limited spaces

name: Pillar Point Harbor (winter south)
notes: Flat-water option on winter storm fronts when S-SSW blows into the harbor; wind is side-off at the beach so stay upwind, because a dropped kite drifts you into the moorings and marina. Gusty prefrontal wind, boat traffic, no summer use (summer NW is ridden on the open beaches to the south). Launch point is unconfirmed; ask locals.
parking: Harbor District lot at the west end of the inner harbor off West Point Ave / Harbor Blvd (by the RV park and west trail); free, shared with surfers and walkers

name: Kings Beach (Lake Tahoe)
notes: North-shore beach that takes the afternoon SW-S wind straight onshore across the whole lake; the most consistent Tahoe launch and where schools teach, so expect beginners on sunny days. Thin air at 6,200 ft (riders run 11-15 m in 15-25 mph), cold water, rocks at the south end at low lake level, swimmers and rental boats in summer; State Parks lists windsurfing but has no posted kite zone.
parking: Kings Beach SRA pay lot off Hwy 28 at Bear St; $10/day or $3/hr year round, card only, state annual pass accepted, lot 6 am-9 pm, no dogs on the beach

name: Folsom Lake - Granite Bay
notes: South-wind (prefrontal) launch, typically cloudy, gusty, 15-28 mph with the iKite sensor reading about 5 mph low; water 46-60 F outside summer so hood and booties. Rocky shoreline and boulders just under the surface, long swim or walk if you go down downwind; rangers are kite-friendly, beginners only on moderate days.
parking: Folsom Lake SRA Granite Bay entrance (Douglas Blvd); $12/vehicle day use, more on peak weekends, annual pass accepted; from the kiosk right at the first stop sign then right at the T, park upwind of the boat ramp

name: Folsom Lake - Folsom Point
notes: North-wind launch: warm, sunny north days blow 19-28 mph (over 30 rare, small kites only) and the sensor is fairly honest up to the 20s. Low water has grown a peninsula with another one about 100 yd downwind, so no big jumps or loops there; rocks eat kites, wind shadow near the lot is where people self-land.
parking: Folsom Lake SRA Folsom Point entrance off E Natoma St; $12/vehicle day use, stay right inside the gate and follow the road to the dead end, longer walk to the water

name: Marina State Beach
notes: Kited on strong NW days (spring clearing winds; summer thermals are light and patchy) but straight onshore, so launching and landing in the shore break is the hard part and locals say do not go out if caution tape is up at the entrance. Heavy beach break, rips, cold water, few local kiters; advanced ocean riders only.
parking: State Beach lot at the west end of Reservation Rd, Marina; free, shared with hang-glider and paraglider pilots
